explanation: p n is the least prime ≡ 1 (mod n) and m n the least k > 0 with n | φ(k), as on erdosproblems.com/456. Question: are there infinitely many primes q such that n = q − 1 is the only n with m_n = q? The statement is that the set of primes q with (m n = q ↔ n = q − 1) is infinite. Faithful.
